description:
src/calendar.rs:184 emits SetErrorType::custom("calendarHasEvents") for the §4.4.1 destroy-with-events rejection. draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §10.7.1 (lines 3297-3302 of references/draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26.txt) registers the wire error name as **calendarHasEvent** (singular). §4.3 of the draft (line 1094) shows the SetError name in the body text as *calendarHasEvent*.

Wire-protocol mismatch: any RFC-compliant client matching on `type == "calendarHasEvent"` will fail to recognize this server's response. The error degrades into an unrecognized-SetError, which clients typically surface as a generic 'serverFail' or unknown-error.

Affected sites in this crate (all need correction together):
- src/calendar.rs:184 (the wire emission — actual bug)
- src/calendar.rs:5, src/calendar.rs:47 (doc comments)
- src/calendar.rs:255, src/calendar.rs:274, src/calendar.rs:275 (test assertion uses wrong string — when fixed, the test will catch the wire bug)
- src/backend.rs:147 (doc comment on calendar_has_events)
- src/lib.rs:618, src/lib.rs:640, src/lib.rs:641 (dispatcher integration test that asserts the wrong string)

Fix: replace 'calendarHasEvents' with 'calendarHasEvent' in the wire emission AND in every test assertion that locks down the wrong value. The test currently passes because it asserts the bug; once the production string is fixed, the test must be updated in the same commit.

Test integrity: the inline tests are not bug-detecting here — they're bug-confirming. Adding a hand-written JSON oracle from the spec (or just asserting against the singular form per §10.7.1) would have caught this. The /review-rusty test-integrity rule applies.

No other JMAP-Calendars-defined SetError type is misspelled in this crate (`forbidden` is a base RFC 8620 type and is spelled correctly; `noSupportedScheduleMethods` is not implemented at all — see separate finding).
title: Calendar/set destroy emits 'calendarHasEvents' (plural); RFC §10.7.1 registers 'calendarHasEvent' (singular)
